documents: Passport plus a second ID or proof of foreign address; SIN not required for a basic account; banks may ask for immigration documents.
min_deposit_fees: Not published for non-residents; fees vary by package and bank.
banks: RBC, TD, Scotiabank, BMO, CIBC (branch opening; newcomer programs target people relocating).
restrictions: Bank Act/FCAC gives anyone with acceptable ID the right to a basic account, but branches usually require an in-person visit; FATCA/CRS reporting applies.
alternatives: Wise CAD account details; Scotiabank/RBC newcomer pre-arrival applications for visa holders.
cost_note: No non-resident tariff published by RBC/TD/Scotiabank/BMO/CIBC (fees vary by package and branches only open for people relocating), and the fee schedule could not be verified this pass, so all figures are null.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, bank reference letter, 6 months of bank statements and source-of-funds evidence; certified/notarised copies if remote.
min_deposit_fees: Reported XCD 100-700 for basic local accounts and USD 10,000-50,000 for international/non-resident accounts (unverified).
banks: Republic Bank, Bank of Nevis, St Kitts-Nevis-Anguilla National Bank, CIBC FirstCaribbean.
restrictions: Enhanced due diligence and higher balances for non-residents; CIBC online opening limited to residents.
alternatives: Wise USD details; regional Caribbean or US accounts.
cost_note: Minimum deposit is the low end of the reported (unverified) USD 10,000-50,000 for international/non-resident accounts at local banks; opening and monthly fees are not published.

documents: Passport, Salvadoran tax number (NIT), description of expected activity; higher-risk clients add income proof or tax returns.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; varies by bank.
banks: Banco Agrícola, Banco Cuscatlán, Davivienda, Promerica (in-person, case by case).
restrictions: 2025 guidelines tier foreign clients by risk; banks look for a local tie (NIT, address, representative); USD is the official currency.
alternatives: Wise USD account; Chivo/Bitcoin wallets outside banking.
cost_note: Banco Agricola, Cuscatlan, Davivienda and Promerica do not publish non-resident opening requirements or fees (case-by-case in branch), so all figures are null.

documents: Passport, foreigner ID card (carnet de extranjero) from temporary residence, NIT, local proof of address.
min_deposit_fees: Reported about USD 50-1,000 (often ~USD 100) initial deposit for residents.
banks: none known for non-residents (Banco Nacional de Bolivia, Mercantil Santa Cruz, BISA serve residents).
restrictions: Tourists cannot open accounts; FX shortages and 2026 currency changes; source-of-funds checks on USD deposits above USD 5,000.
alternatives: Wise or home-country accounts; local cash.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here, so all cost fields are null; resident accounts reportedly need about USD 50-1,000 (often ~USD 100) initial deposit.

documents: Residence card (zairyu card), registered Japanese address, Japanese phone number, hanko or signature.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; ordinary accounts usually free.
banks: none known for non-residents (Japan Post Bank, Rakuten, Shinsei/SBI serve residence-card holders).
restrictions: Under the FX Act foreigners in Japan under 6 months are non-residents; tourists cannot open accounts and non-resident yen accounts are heavily restricted.
alternatives: Wise JPY account details for receiving funds.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here, so all cost fields are null; ordinary accounts for residence-card holders are usually free.

documents: Passport with visa, often a work permit or long-term visa, immigration residence certificate or embassy letter, Thai phone number.
min_deposit_fees: UOB non-resident accounts reportedly need THB 50,000; others small or not published.
banks: Bangkok Bank, Kasikorn, SCB, UOB (branch discretion; tourists sometimes accepted).
restrictions: Bank of Thailand rules on non-resident baht accounts and anti-fraud tightening; practice varies by branch.
alternatives: Wise THB details; DTV/long-stay visa first.
cost_note: Bangkok Bank FCD savings account for non-residents (fee schedule effective 1 Oct 2018): USD 1,000 initial deposit, USD 10/month charged only if the average balance falls below USD 250 (so 0 if maintained); no opening fee is published.

documents: Passport, NZ visa (residence/work/student), overseas address, IRD number or home tax declaration.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; standard accounts typically low or no fee.
banks: ASB, ANZ, BNZ, Kiwibank (pre-arrival accounts for migrants).
restrictions: Pre-arrival accounts are limited until in-branch ID verification; programs aimed at people moving with a visa.
alternatives: Wise NZD account details.
cost_note: ASB everyday/Streamline account carries NZD 0 monthly fee with electronic statements per third-party migrant guides (not confirmed on ASB's tariff); opening fee and minimum deposit are not published.

documents: Passport, local Funafuti address, visa or work permit (reported).
min_deposit_fees: Reported about AUD 50 minimum deposit (unverified).
banks: National Bank of Tuvalu (only commercial bank).
restrictions: No central bank; uses AUD; correspondent banking ties to Australia at risk per IMF; in-person only.
alternatives: Keep Australian bank accounts (AUD is legal tender).
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here, so all cost fields are null; National Bank of Tuvalu reportedly asks about AUD 50 (~USD 33 at 0.66) minimum deposit from residents (unverified).

documents: Passport, visa/registration, local presence; banks may refuse at discretion.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: none known (state banks such as Senagat, Dayhanbank, State Bank for Foreign Economic Affairs).
restrictions: State-owned banking, strict currency controls, separate TMT and USD/EUR accounts, foreigners rarely onboarded.
alternatives: none
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here, so all cost fields are null; state banks publish no tariff for foreigners.

documents: Passport, proof of address, residence permit if any, tax ID if available, initial deposit.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: BGFIBank Gabon, Ecobank, UBA (non-residents finalise at branch or via power of attorney).
restrictions: CEMAC/BEAC exchange rules; non-resident foreign-currency accounts allowed but cannot go overdrawn.
alternatives: Mobile money (Airtel Money, Moov Money) needs local SIM; Wise for sending.
cost_note: BGFIBank, Ecobank and UBA Gabon do not publish non-resident opening deposits or account-keeping fees, and the tariff could not be retrieved this pass, so all figures are null.

documents: Passport, residence or investor status, landlord attestation, JIRAMA utility bill, photos.
min_deposit_fees: BNI reportedly MGA 400,000 minimum deposit (old forum report).
banks: none known for non-residents (BNI, BOA, BFV/Societe Generale Madagasikara, BMOI serve residents).
restrictions: Foreigners need established residence or investor status; physical presence required; French-language service.
alternatives: Mobile money (MVola, Orange Money) with local SIM.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here, so all cost fields are null; BNI reportedly required MGA 400,000 (~USD 90 at 4,500/USD) minimum deposit from residents per an old forum report.

documents: Passport or work permit, proof of residential address, source of funds, employment/income proof, tax details.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: none known for non-residents (Standard Lesotho Bank Pro tier open to foreigners with full KYC).
restrictions: Common Monetary Area with South Africa; KYC assumes local address; Standard Bank SA excludes Lesotho residents from its non-resident accounts.
alternatives: South African bank accounts; M-Pesa/EcoCash with local SIM.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here, so all cost fields are null; Standard Lesotho Bank tariffs apply only to customers with full local KYC.

documents: Passport, proof of address, bank reference, detailed source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, tax self-certification.
min_deposit_fees: Reported CHF 100,000-500,000 at LLB and around CHF/EUR 1 million at LGT or VP Bank (unverified).
banks: LGT, Liechtensteinische Landesbank (LLB), VP Bank.
restrictions: Private-banking model with high minimums; CRS/FATCA reporting; US persons restricted.
alternatives: Swiss private banks; Wise CHF/EUR accounts.
cost_note: Minimum is the low end of the reported (unverified) CHF 100,000-500,000 at LLB converted at ~1.25 USD/CHF (LGT/VP Bank reportedly ~CHF/EUR 1 million); opening and monthly fees are not published.

documents: Passport and Croatian tax number (OIB, issued at a tax office on presentation of passport); sometimes proof of foreign address.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; small or no opening deposit at most banks.
banks: PBZ, Zagrebacka banka, Erste, Raiffeisen (RBA), OTP.
restrictions: Non-resident accounts available with OIB; branch visit usually required; euro area since 2023.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut (EUR IBAN).
cost_note: PBZ euro current account fee EUR 1.61/month per its April 2026 tariff for domestic and foreign individuals (first fee charged 90 days after opening; digital banking EUR 1.59/month extra), converted at ~1.16 USD/EUR; no opening fee or minimum deposit is published.

documents: Passport, proof of foreign address, possibly Romanian tax ID (CIF/NIF) and source-of-funds info.
min_deposit_fees: Reported a few hundred to a few thousand RON depending on bank.
banks: BCR, Banca Transilvania, Raiffeisen Bank Romania.
restrictions: Remote app-based opening mostly aimed at Romanians abroad; foreigners usually visit a branch.
alternatives: Revolut, Wise (EUR/RON details).
cost_note: Banca Transilvania's individual fee sheet lists RON 0 monthly administration for a lei current account (resident terms; non-resident tariff not separately published); minimum deposit is only reported vaguely as a few hundred to a few thousand RON, so null.

documents: Passport, registered Finnish address, residence permit or proof of residence; Finnish ID code not legally required for basic services.
min_deposit_fees: Not published; basic accounts carry monthly fees.
banks: Nordea, OP, Danske Bank (in practice require Finnish address).
restrictions: Basic-banking right covers EEA residents; banks usually require a Finnish registered address; strong e-ID not given without Finnish ID.
alternatives: Wise, Revolut, or EU online banks.
cost_note: Nordea Finland basic current account EUR 2.60/month from 1 May 2026 (access codes EUR 0.99 and debit card EUR 2.99 extra), converted at ~1.16 USD/EUR; no opening fee or minimum deposit is published.

documents: Only eligible categories (Catholic institutions, clergy, Vatican employees/pensioners, diplomats accredited to the Holy See).
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: none (the IOR does not accept ordinary foreign individuals).
restrictions: IOR closed lay accounts that fall outside its categories; residents and visitors use Italian banks in Rome.
alternatives: Italian banks or EU fintechs (Wise, Revolut).
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here, so all cost fields are null; the IOR does not accept ordinary foreign individuals.

documents: Passport with UAE entry stamp, proof of foreign address, 6 months of bank statements, bank reference letter, proof of income/source of funds.
min_deposit_fees: Reported AED 3,000-5,000 at Emirates NBD and AED 25,000+ at Mashreq for non-residents; some banks AED 100,000+.
banks: Emirates NBD, Mashreq, ADCB, RAKBANK, FAB.
restrictions: Non-resident accounts usually savings-type with no chequebook or credit; at least one branch visit common; strict AML checks.
alternatives: Wise AED details; UAE digital banks require Emirates ID.
cost_note: Emirates NBD current account (Key Fact Statement): AED 3,000 minimum average balance (~USD 817 at 3.6725 AED/USD) with an AED 26.25 (~USD 7.15) monthly fall-below fee only if under that balance, so 0 if maintained; no opening fee is published.

documents: Passport, sometimes a Tunisian address, declaration of other accounts; customs declaration of imported foreign cash.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: BNA, Amen Bank, STB, ABC Bank, UBCI, Attijari Bank.
restrictions: Non-residents may freely open foreign-currency or convertible-dinar accounts without BCT approval; ordinary dinar accounts are subject to exchange controls.
alternatives: Wise for transfers; few fintech options locally.
cost_note: BNA, Amen Bank, STB and others do not publish a non-resident (convertible dinar) account tariff that could be retrieved this pass, so all figures are null.

documents: Passport, residence or work permit, local address, in-person KYC.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: none known for non-residents (KCB, Equity Bank operate in Juba for residents and organisations).
restrictions: Conflict-affected, severe currency instability and USD shortages; de-risking by correspondents.
alternatives: Mobile money (m-Gurush, MTN MoMo) with local SIM; hawala.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here, so all cost fields are null; KCB and Equity Bank serve only residents and organisations.

documents: Passport, Afghan visa and local presence; Tazkira for locals.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: none known for non-residents.
restrictions: Taliban-run central bank under sanctions pressure; weekly withdrawal caps; most foreign correspondents refuse transfers.
alternatives: Western Union, MoneyGram (up to USD 5,000 per transaction), hawala.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here, so all cost fields are null.

documents: Passport with visa or residence card, proof of local accommodation or residence certificate, in-person KYC.
min_deposit_fees: not published
banks: none known for non-residents (Ecobank Guinee, BICIGUI, Orabank, AFG Bank serve residents).
restrictions: Exchange controls on Guinean francs; branch visit and local residence documents expected.
alternatives: Orange Money/MTN MoMo with local SIM.
cost_note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here, so all cost fields are null; local banks serve residents only.

documents: Passport, Cabo Verdean tax number (NIF, issued at a Casa do Cidadao), local address and phone, signed opening form.
min_deposit_fees: Minimum opening deposit varies by bank; not published.
banks: Caixa Economica de Cabo Verde, BCA, Banco InterAtlantico, Ecobank.
restrictions: Non-residents and tourists can open accounts but no standard fully remote route; cards collected at branch; escudo pegged to euro.
alternatives: Wise EUR account for transfers.
cost_note: Caixa Economica, BCA, Banco InterAtlantico and Ecobank do not publish non-resident minimum deposits or maintenance fees retrievable this pass, so all figures are null.
